id_and_class.summary: Schopenhauer holds that the world has two aspects: representation, the world of objects structured by space, time, and causality for a knowing subject, and will, a single blind, aimless striving that is the inner essence of everything. We know the will directly in one case only, our own body felt from within as willing. Consciousness and intellect are secondary tools the will develops in higher organisms, so phenomenal experience is a surface over a non-conscious reality.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Will's Secondary Instrument

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is representation, the subject-object field of appearances, produced by the brain as an instrument of the will. Underneath it lies will, the non-conscious thing-in-itself.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The body is given twice: outwardly as one represented object among others and inwardly as felt will. Volitions do not cause bodily acts; they are those acts grasped from within.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Consciousness arises only at higher grades of the will's objectification, as a biological tool the will produces, while the will itself is primitive and non-conscious.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Every object exists only for a subject, so experience is intrinsically correlational. Ordinary self-transparency is an illusion, since much of what moves us is willing hidden from the intellect.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Schopenhauer offers no theory of qualia. Felt willing is the one non-representational access to how things are in themselves; the rest of experience is representation shaped by space, time, and causality.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: One undivided will as thing-in-itself; a knowing subject; representations structured by space, time, causality, and the principle of sufficient reason; the brain as organ of representation.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Outer, objective knowledge reaches only appearances. Inner awareness of one's own willing body is the single window onto reality as it is in itself.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A two-sided world. As representation it is a multiplicity of individuated objects; as will it is one, and space and time (the principles of individuation) fragment it into many phenomena.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Perceptual and cognitive representation; affect and desire; self-knowledge; the place of consciousness in nature.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Double knowledge of the body. Generalizing from felt willing, Schopenhauer concludes that the inner essence of all phenomena, organic and inorganic, is will.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness appears at higher stages of the will's objectification and can be extinguished in sleep, injury, or death while the will persists.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Will is everywhere as the essence of all things. Consciousness is confined to higher organisms with brains.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The intellect serves the will's striving. Schopenhauer pictures the will as a blind, powerful giant carrying a sighted but weak dwarf, the intellect, on its shoulders.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Representation unifies appearances under space, time, and causality for a single subject; the will is unified in itself and only appears divided.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The principle of sufficient reason governs relations among objects, concepts, mathematical constructions, and motives, but representation never reveals the inner nature of things.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Intellect and consciousness are instruments the will develops in higher organisms to serve its striving, a view that anticipates evolutionary and depth-psychological accounts of mind.
core_claims_and_evidence: The world is my representation: every object exists only as an object for a subject.
Each person knows one object, their own body, both as representation and immediately as will.
The will is the thing-in-itself, a single blind striving underlying all phenomena.
Consciousness is derivative and serves the will, which acts largely beyond the intellect's view.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical argument building on Kant, grounded in inner experience of willing.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Since the will is known only in one's own case, inferring that all other phenomena are will faces a generalization problem and, if resisted, threatens solipsism. Scholars such as Christopher Janaway and Robert Wicks note dispute over whether Schopenhauer identifies the will with the Kantian thing-in-itself or only with the thing-in-itself as it appears to inner sense.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The view aims to demote consciousness and does not explain phenomenal qualities. How a non-conscious will gives rise to conscious representation is left as a fact about higher organisms.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Departs from Kant by claiming inner access to the thing-in-itself. His intrinsic-nature strategy anticipates Russellian monism and panpsychism, though because the will is explicitly non-conscious he is a forerunner of panpsychism and not a panpsychist about consciousness.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Schopenhauer ties consciousness to brains in higher organisms produced by the will. He says nothing about whether an artificial system could serve as such an instrument.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Consciousness is extinguished at death; only the non-conscious, impersonal will persists.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The will at the root of reality is blind and aimless, so the cosmos has no purpose. Any relief lies in human aesthetic contemplation, compassion, and renunciation of willing.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Since conscious individuality is a passing appearance of the one will, preserving a copy of a mind would not preserve anything essential.
